spec_match.rationale: Concepts map the exact current W3C Window Management Working Draft (TR publication dated 2026-07-14): minimize()/maximize()/restore() complete asynchronously via the 'request a window display state change' algorithm, with NotAllowedError paths for policy disallowance, a non-installed document, missing transient activation, denied permission, or failed operation; setResizable() has its separate algorithm without the transient-activation check; §3.6.1 display-state and §3.6.2 resizable media features, explicitly NOT permission-gated) without collapsing in the sibling Window Management surface (getScreenDetails/ScreenDetailed/fullscreen options/PiP/popup placement — none of which this family claims). The resizable semantics are verified against the explainer: non-user-resizable windows block user drag/keyboard/frame/menu resizing while Web APIs (resizeTo(), maximize(), requestFullscreen()) still work.

interactive.rationale: Real Promise-returning calls on explicit buttons with resolution AND rejection both reported (missing method, no permission, not an installed app, unsupported), live media-feature readouts with change listeners, and a separate Fullscreen API control with :fullscreen feedback that is never presented as target evidence. No auto permission requests, no popups, no simulated grants/multi-screen/OS movement.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Parent corrected current-shipment wording and cards to match the proposal: the stable v150 route is not a Chrome 150 shipment claim, the W3C document is a Working Draft, and gating is separated: runtime availability controls exposure; installed-app/policy/permission checks govern all four calls; transient activation additionally governs minimize/maximize/restore but not setResizable. Note on listing state: the chromestatus detail (updated 2026-07-24 20:34 UTC — after the folder was built on 2026-07-18) currently records 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' with desktop=None and no milestone, and the feature id is not present in any current milestone listing (checked v150–v155 on 2026-07-25); the v150 route is the folder's historical identity from the 2026-07-18 build and is preserved under the durable contract, with current listing reality stated here rather than hidden.

edge_cases.rationale: Honest negatives throughout: absent methods reported (never faked), media features judged only by actual exhaustive value matches because unknown media-query text can serialize unchanged, fullscreen exercises only the separate Fullscreen API and :fullscreen pseudo-class, and no claim that a permission result proves multi-screen hardware, popup allowance, placement success, fullscreen, or OS/window-manager cooperation. A successful resizeTo() call is not presented as evidence of resizing while locked unless (resizable: false) actively matches.

references.rationale: All pages cite chromestatus.com/feature/5201832664629248, the W3C Window Management Working Draft (TR publication dated 2026-07-14) (method anchors verified: #api-window-minimize-method/#api-window-maximize-method/#api-window-restore-method/#api-window-setresizable-method/#descdef-media-display-state/#descdef-media-resizable), and the googlers' AWC explainer (resizable semantics + permission requirements verified verbatim); the index also links the Google AWC demo app and MDN's Fullscreen API page. Runtime feature verified: DesktopPWAsAdditionalWindowingControls (experimental, origin_trial_feature_name same, origin_trial_os win/mac/linux/chromeos, third-party allowed, base_feature_status enabled).

conformance.rationale: New immutable root suite has 9 direct contracts: four exact Window-instance method exposures and two exhaustive media-value behavior checks fail honestly, while three effect/event contracts are manual/blocked (state-method resolution/rejection and genuine transition, setResizable resolution plus media-state change, and display-state change events). Parent removed the always-green not-static trap and replaced both false parse passes: matchMedia() preserves unknown feature text, so conformance now requires exactly one exhaustive value to match. Chrome 150 renders exactly 0 pass / 6 fail / 3 blocked.

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp on HeadlessChrome/150 (2026-07-25): all safe controls exercised at 1280×800 and 390×844 with post-interaction geometry — probe grid reports all four methods undefined + 'none of the window-state methods are exposed here' honest fallback without assuming that installation alone explains absence, buttons report unavailable without fake results, display-state reports that no value matches and explicitly says query serialization is not support evidence, while the separate Fullscreen API control and :fullscreen feedback are labelled non-target behavior. resizable-lock reports no active media value instead of falsely calling the window locked, and resizeTo() success is not attributed to a fixed state that was never established; clear-log works, zero console errors and zero failed requests. No permission, popup, or window operation was auto-issued.

telemetry_health.rationale: Concepts emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events per branch (awc-window-methods-probe, awc-<method>-unavailable/resolved/rejected, awc-display-state-observed, awc-resizable-observed, and explicitly separate fullscreen-state telemetry); telemetry POSTs returned 202 during validation.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, button background+color pairs, focus-visible outlines, no static-card pattern; edits were suite/critique level with one index copy fix and preserve layout.

accessibility.rationale: role=log/aria-live on the results log and state readouts, probed cells expose values as text, buttons are native and keyboard-operable with visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Matrix pass including post-interaction states: all five pages scrollWidth equals viewport at 1280×800 and 390×844 after every safe control (probe, invoke, clear, separate fullscreen control).

openQuestions.title: Verify resolution contracts in an installed PWA with the flag and real permission UI
openQuestions.detail: This build (browser tab, flag off) exposes none of the four methods and no display-state or resizable value matches. Query text is preserved even for an invented media feature, so parsing/serialization was not counted as support; only honest method-absence paths and the separate Fullscreen API control and :fullscreen feedback were exercised. In an installed desktop PWA with DesktopPWAsAdditionalWindowingControls enabled and the window-management permission granted via browser UI, verify: each state method resolves and the display-state value flips accordingly; setResizable(false) flips (resizable: false) while resizeTo() keeps working (per the explainer's semantics); transient-activation and installed-app rejections are NotAllowedError per the TR's algorithm; and the display-state change event fires on genuine transitions. Also re-check the feature's listing placement — as of 2026-07-25 it is in no milestone listing while the detail says dev trial with no desktop milestone.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region announcements for dynamic probe/status results after button activation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamic state through live regions tied to the activating control; expose results as text with programmatic roles.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verified applied: the results log is role=log aria-live, state readouts update live, probe cells are text values.

guidanceConsulted.query: permission-gated window management APIs that require real browser UI mediation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Powerful platform features must be user-initiated through real browser UI; never simulate grants, hardware, or OS cooperation.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied strictly: no auto permission requests or popups anywhere; all four window-state methods are only invoked on explicit buttons; the suite's resolution contracts are manual-blocked rather than simulated; the separate Fullscreen API is the only state change exercised, via explicit browser-mediated fullscreen UI, and is not counted as target evidence.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: interaction log — zero permission/popup requests outside explicit clicks; suite renders 3 blocked

summary: Source-review of the Additional Windowing Controls family against the W3C Window Management Working Draft published 2026-07-14 (minimize/maximize/restore use the asynchronous display-state-change algorithm, including NotAllowedError paths for policy, installation, permission, activation, or failed OS operation; setResizable has its separate no-transient-activation algorithm; display-state + resizable media features, both permission-free), the AWC explainer (permission requirements + resizable semantics verified verbatim), the direct chromestatus detail (updated 2026-07-24 20:34 UTC: currently 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)', desktop=None, no milestone — and the id is in no current milestone listing as of 2026-07-25, a volatile listing state recorded honestly; the folder was built 2026-07-18 and keeps its v150 identity under the durable contract), and the runtime feature DesktopPWAsAdditionalWindowingControls (experimental; origin_trial_os win/mac/linux/chromeos; third-party allowed). The submitted family appeared layer-accurate, but parent found false media-query feature detection, current-shipment copy, adjacent fullscreen claims, and resize-state causality defects; the corrected family keeps layers accurate (methods vs media features vs permission vs installed-app vs activation vs OS cooperation kept separate; no PiP/popup/getScreenDetails conflation). Added the immutable root suite; parent removed one negative binding pass and replaced two false media-parse passes with exhaustive behavior checks, leaving 9 direct contracts: 6 fail / 3 blocked / 0 pass. Missing-suite denominator 2→1 expected (797/798).
